brief: UBS sales commentary reframes Thursday's US equity selloff as a correlation story, not just a sector rotation: index-level moves are now emerging on top of the rotations already underway, and the absence of long-only buyers (unlike July) is a key risk even though leverage starts cleaner. Three capitulation signals (record $365bn excess sell flow, a 96% VIX Cross-Asset Rank, roughly $170-210bn of Thursday systematic selling) lead UBS to expect SPX to bottom Monday as Risk Control and CTA flows fade, consistent with technicals arguing the selloff is corrective and supporting an 8,485 SPX target next year. A separate note argues the market may be conflating data-centre regulation fears, sparked by Democratic midterm sweeps in Texas and Georgia, with an outright halt, and sees different implications for infrastructure suppliers. US payrolls data stays soft but not alarming: claims fell, the payroll forecast was lifted to 75K, and productivity/unit labor cost data reinforce that labor is not the main inflation driver. The note also reports, without further analysis, items on Banxico, Germany data, French political instability, the NZ election, Japanese wages, GPIF and BoJ ETF sales.
